subject: Request: GPU class equivalency and cost-share for Dedicated Reserve
messages:
From: Samir Desai <ops@neuroforge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Reddy <finance@neuroforge.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reserve request: H200 parity for H100 / cost-share idea

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the deep-dive yesterday. Quick summary from our side and a formal ask so you can route it to the right folks:

- Background: NeuroForge is committing to a 12-month Dedicated reserve (target Q4 start). Our inference workload is tuned to H100-family profiles, but supply in our preferred region is constrained.

- Ask: We would like Redwood to accept an H200-class accelerator (different family) as a capacity-equivalent for the committed reserved pool for the first 6 months. Operationally we will accept the H200 if Redwood can guarantee a 95th%-tile latency parity SLA for our canonical prompt set and provide kernel-level tuning (we understand this is non-standard).

- Commercial: We propose a cost-share model for the transient performance delta: NeuroForge will cover incremental overage at a blended 50% share (NeuroForge) / 50% (Redwood) for any delta above baseline token cost for the first 3 months; after that we re-evaluate. Additionally, we request a one-time 7% commitment discount to offset migration risk.

Attached is our Q4 demand forecast and a short appendix with latency targets.

Can you confirm feasibility and, if needed, escalate for an executive exception on GPU-family acceptance and the blended overage share?

Best,
Samir Desai
Head of Platform Operations
NeuroForge

Attachments: NeuroForge_Demand_Forecast_Q4.xlsx
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Deals Desk <deals@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 11:04:37 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reserve request: H200 parity for H100 / cost-share idea

Forwarding Samir's note — Needing quick alignment and exec sign-off guidance. Highlights:

- External asks an H200-class accelerator to be accepted as an equivalent for a 12-month Dedicated commit in their preferred region for the first 6 months.
- They want a 95th%-tile latency parity guarantee for canonical prompts (will require some runtime/compiled-kernel work).
- Commercial: blended overage cost-share (50/50) for first 3 months + one-time 7% commitment discount.

My read: technically feasible with a targeted kernel/compilation plan, but this is a non-standard GPU-family acceptance + non-standard commercial concession (discount + shared overage). We need executive sign-off for: 1) non-standard GPU acceptance (carrier substitution) and 2) temporary overage sharing + discounted commit.

Requested actions:
- Karthik: can you draft a short concession framework (limits, expiry, guardrails)?
- Lauren: is 7% one-time within the exec approval band or does this need CRO/CFO sign-off?
- Marcus: please confirm whether SRE/serving runtime can meet a 95th%-tile latency parity attestation if we schedule kernel tuning now (approx 4-6 week engineering run).

I have attached their forecast (from Samir) and a suggested rate-card markups doc.

Thanks — we need a decision before Friday close of business to lock the Q4 start.

--
Olga Petrov
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: NeuroForge_Demand_Forecast_Q4.xlsx, proposed-rate-card-v2.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Sep 2028 08:27:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated reserve request: H200 parity for H100 / cost-share idea

Thanks for the context, Olga. Quick framework suggestion for a clean exec decision:

1) Technical gating: Accept H200-family as a temporary equivalent on following conditions:
   - SRE completes a kernel/compilation tuning run and provides a performance attestation for their canonical prompt set within 6 weeks.
   - If parity (95th%-tile latency within 10% of H100 baseline) is not met by 6 weeks, Redwood may revert traffic to compatible variants or apply a pre-agreed incremental overage surcharge.

2) Commercial guardrails:
   - One-time commitment discount: cap at 5% (not 7%). Anything above 5% requires CRO sign-off.
   - Blended overage share: Redwood covers 25% of incremental overage for months 0-3; NeuroForge covers 75%. This lowers Redwood exposure while signaling partnership.
   - Cap on total make-good exposure: Redwood liability limited to $75k over the 3-month window.

3) Timebox & review: 90-day trial with a formal post-trial review and possible amendment to committed sku mapping.

If Lauren is comfortable with the 5% cap and the $75k liability, I'm happy to pull together a simple amendment for the Deals Desk and a DocuSign envelope.

-Karthik
Head of Enterprise Deals
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated reserve request: H200 parity for H100 / cost-share idea

Thanks team — decision and next steps below.

Approval (executive exception granted, with the following edits):
- One-time commitment discount approved at 5% (Karthik recommendation). No further reduction without CRO/CFO review.
- Blended overage share adjusted to Redwood 30% / Customer 70% for months 0-3. Redwood exposure capped at $60k for the trial window.
- Technical gating stands: SRE must produce the attestation within 6 weeks; if attestation fails, we revert to fallback SKUs or apply the pre-agreed surcharge.

Operational next steps (Deals Desk / Legal / SRE):
1) Deals Desk: prepare an amendment for DF-91827 reflecting the 5% one-time commit discount, 30/70 overage split, $60k cap, and 90-day trial. Include the kernel-attestation SLA clause and rollback policy. Please route to DocuSign and Cc me.
2) SRE (Marcus): prioritize kernel tuning work and run the attestation campaign within 6 weeks — share test harness and results with NeuroForge and Legal.
3) Olga: confirm NeuroForge accepts the 30/70 split and $60k cap; if they push back, pause DocuSign and escalate.

Olga — you have exec sign-off. Karthik, Deals Desk, Marcus — please action.

-Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
